pages.text: MC3DPrint has no required dependencies. Every mod below is a $(l)soft$() dependency: if you have it, MC3DPrint knows about it.$(br2)If you do not, nothing happens at all: no crash, no warnings, no stray config. An absent mod is invisible.

Most modded items get a $(l)Filament Unit$() value for free. MC3DPrint reads ordinary crafting and smelting recipes, so a mod's whole tree usually prices itself from a few raw materials.$(br2)What it $(l)cannot$() read is a custom machine: a Smeltery alloy, an Inscriber press. Those get pinned by hand.
pages.title: Values Come For Free

pages.text: Pinned values follow the same $(l)abundance rule$() as everything else: a material cannot sit at a tier whose spool could print something rarer than the material itself.$(br2)That is why a farmable alloy lands near iron and a Nether-mined one lands near blaze rods, regardless of how expensive its own mod considers it.
pages.title: The Abundance Rule

pages.text: Two mods change what MC3DPrint can $(l)do$(), not just what things cost:$(br2)$(l)Applied Energistics 2$() adds the MC3DPrint Terminal.$(br2)$(l)Draconic Evolution$() unlocks the Tier 8 Fabricator.$(br2)Everything else contributes material values.
pages.title: Two Are Different

pages.text: Cross-mod materials are kept $(l)level$(). Steel is steel whether Tinkers', Ender IO or Immersive Engineering made it, so the same material cannot be arbitraged from one mod into another.$(br2)Anything left $(l)unvalued$() is refused by strict mode rather than printed for free.
pages.title: No Arbitrage
